extraction_scope: Worker-5 re-review replaced automated pending-review locator notes with source-reviewed mechanism ontology claims. No claim is promoted to direct_mechanism because the local paper does not provide a direct virion-binding, fusion, permeability, or target-binding assay for GF19.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: GF19 pre-treatment blocked or strongly reduced HSV-1 infection in HCECs and ex vivo mouse cornea, while treatment immediately after infection attenuated but did not arrest infection; this supports a likely viral-entry/preventive effect rather than virucidal clearance.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: GF19 against HSV-1 McKrae in human corneal epithelial cells and ex vivo mouse cornea

source_locator.locator: xml:abstract; xml:sec=9:Antiviral efficacy of GF19 against HSV-1; fig=4B; pdf_text:41598_2024_Article_53662.txt:430-551

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source uses timing and immunofluorescence/plaque phenotypes to infer likely entry blocking. It does not include a direct HSV-1 binding, envelope disruption, fusion, or entry-receptor assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: GF19 was designed by adding C-terminal lysine/leucine and amidation to GF17, with in-silico reactivity and membrane-propensity analyses used as rationale for improved membrane interaction and antiviral potential.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: GF19 peptide design and in-silico structure/reactivity model

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:GF-19 peptide design; xml:sec=7:In silico testing of GF19; pdf_text:41598_2024_Article_53662.txt:306-320,322-386

mechanism_claims.limitations: Hydrophobicity, KL addition, rGb, MPr, and PyMol/BRANEart outputs are design/model evidence. They are not direct experimental proof that GF19 ruptures HSV-1 membranes.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SiNP encapsulation of GF19 is supported as a delivery context that sustained or enhanced the observed anti-HSV-1 effect in HCECs, with SiNP-GF19-treated cells retaining more attached/intact morphology at 48 h than free GF19 or untreated infected cells.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=10:Encapsulation of GF19 in silica NPs; xml:sec=11:GF19 interaction with human corneal epithelial cells; fig=5; fig=6; pdf_text:41598_2024_Article_53662.txt:552-704

mechanism_claims.limitations: The local evidence supports delivery/sustained-release phenotype and physicochemical encapsulation, not a distinct direct antiviral molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: GF19 partially activated BMDC inflammatory markers, with TNF-alpha and CD40 comparable to LPS but without increased CD80/CD86 costimulatory ligand expression; this is host-response compatibility context, not direct HSV-1 mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: GF19 treatment of mouse bone marrow-derived dendritic cells

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:Biocompatibility and immune compatibility of GF19; fig=3B; pdf_text:41598_2024_Article_53662.txt:400-427

mechanism_claims.limitations: BMDC marker changes are immune compatibility/host response data. They must not be promoted to direct antiviral mechanism.
